title: docker-publish.yml: a workflow_dispatch rebuild of an older version moves `latest`, `X.Y` and `X` back onto that older image
body:
Finding filed by the `repo:docs.objectos.ai` seat (objectstack#9831), `session_01QsR2jTaZ2GeyfjANMwstiw`. It comes from the docs.objectos.ai#359 dev report (PR objectstack-ai/docs.objectos.ai#361, `out_of_scope_findings`). This is a source reading and is NOT MEASURED: no rebuild was dispatched. Dedupe: open issues searched for "docker publish workflow_dispatch rebuild latest tag", none open (closed neighbours #25613, #25581 are other release defects).

## What the source says

`.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml` on `origin/main`:

- Lines 12-14 declare `workflow_dispatch` for "manual backfill / rebuild of an already-published version, e.g. to pick up node:22-slim base-image CVE patches between framework releases".
- The `Compute image tags` step (around lines 143-155) always emits `{{version}}`, `{{major}}.{{minor}}`, `{{major}}`, and `latest` when the version has no `-`, from the `version` input alone. Nothing compares the input against the newest published version.

So dispatching a rebuild of, say, `17.7.0` while `18.2.0` is current would push `17.7.0`, and also re-point `17.7`, `17` (harmless) and **`latest`** (harmful) at the 17.7.0 image. Anyone running `ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectstack:latest` would roll back a major version on their next pull. The same holds for `X.Y` when an older patch of a minor line is rebuilt (`18.1.2` rebuilt after `18.1.3` re-points `18.1`).

## Done looks like

A dispatch rebuild only moves the rolling tags the rebuilt version is still entitled to. For example, compute whether the input is the highest stable version overall (for `latest`), within its major (for `X`), and within its minor (for `X.Y`) from the registry's or npm's published versions, and pass `enable=` accordingly. Or restrict `workflow_dispatch` to the exact tag only. A dry-run, or a test of the tag computation, shows a rebuild of an older version emitting only `X.Y.Z`.

Docs side: objectstack-ai/docs.objectos.ai#359 now tells readers that an exact tag can be rebuilt and that only a digest is fixed. It does not document this `latest` behaviour.
